findings.summary: parseAnyBranchShape (lease mode) accepts two refspec forms the leaseOnOwnBranch parser deliberately refuses, and omits the refAliasState check. (1) No-colon refspecs (`origin docs/x`, `origin HEAD`) are accepted with dst = src, but git maps a no-colon src through remote.<name>.push, so the push can land elsewhere: after `git config remote.origin.push refs/heads/docs/x:refs/heads/main`, `git push --force-with-lease origin docs/x` is allowed by the hook yet force-pushes main. Unprotected DEFAULT_PROTECTED names (gh-pages, release-please--branches--*, prod) are exposed the same way. (2) Unqualified colon destinations (`HEAD:v0.26.0`) are resolved by git against the remote, tags before heads, so `git push --force-with-lease=v0.26.0:<sha> origin HEAD:v0.26.0` passes isPlainBranchName and rewrites a release tag. Fix: in lease mode require the colon form with a fully qualified refs/heads/<branch> destination, refuse no-colon refspecs and bare destinations (or enforce refAliasState and reject when remote.<remote>.push is set), and add these cases to enforce-lease-any-branch.test.mjs; current tests explicitly allow `origin some-branch`, `origin HEAD` and `-u origin HEAD`.
